name: BORGHESAN
description: Concurred, argued that Initiative 2 does not violate political parties' associational rights, the constitutional provisions for electing the lieutenant governor, or the constitutional provisions for electing the governor.

name: BORGHESAN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the allotment and ILP statutes are not facially unconstitutional because they have a plainly legitimate sweep with many permissible uses, and the superior court erred in striking them down entirely.

name: BORGHESAN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Alaska Constitution permits the use of a preponderance of the evidence standard in prison disciplinary proceedings and that the argument regarding saliva tests was waived.

name: Carney, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the city ordinance limiting trapping in certain areas for public safety and land use is not impliedly prohibited by state law and does not conflict with the state's authority over natural resources.

name: BORGHESAN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Alaska Constitution requires law enforcement to obtain a warrant before using aircraft and vision-enhancing technology to observe a home's curtilage protected from ground-level view.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the court's decision is too narrow and that Alaskans' reasonable expectation of privacy in the home and curtilage requires a warrant for any targeted aerial surveillance, with or without technological enhancements.

name: CARNEY, Justice
description: Concurred with Justice Maassen's opinion, arguing for a broader protection of privacy against aerial surveillance.

name: Henderson, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Armstrong established Alaska residency on May 20, 2019, by being physically present with the intent to remain indefinitely and make her home, and her subsequent actions were consistent with this intent.

name: Carney, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that Armstrong did not establish residency before June 1, 2019, and the court's interpretation of residency requirements could allow almost any tourist to become a state resident.

name: BORGHESAN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that OCS was not required to follow civil commitment statutes but that the 46-day wait for a hearing on a child's psychiatric hospitalization violated procedural due process.

name: CARNEY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the superior court's decisions regarding the constitutional claim, preliminary injunction, and attorney's fees should be affirmed.

name: WINFREE, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the attorney's fees decision was affirmed based on how it was litigated, but believed the Tribe's premise about constitutional claimant framework and Rule 82 interrelation was mistaken regarding the State.

name: Maassen, Justice
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: Borghesan, Justice
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: Winfree, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General's suit was an action brought 'in the name of the State against the legislature' and was therefore forbidden by Article III, Section 16 of the Alaska Constitution, reinforcing the constitutional balance of power.

name: Carney, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the superior court's findings on Williams's liability for contamination, damages, and contribution were affirmed, with a remand for more specific injunctive relief.

name: Borghesan, Justice
description: Did not participate in the case.

name: Henderson, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the State's detentions of Abigail and Jethro violated their substantive due process rights because the restrictive nature and long duration of their detentions were not reasonably related to the limited purpose of transporting them for emergency evaluation.

name: Eastaugh, Senior Justice
description: Concurred, but expressed doubts about the *Hickel v. Southeast Conference* priorities for applying contiguity, compactness, and socio-economic integration criteria, though these doubts did not affect the outcome of the petitions.

name: BORGHESAN, JUSTICE.
description: Concurred, argued that AS 09.55.548(b) violates the equal protection clause of the Alaska Constitution when applied to claimants whose collateral source has a contractual right to reimbursement, as the distinctions drawn by the statute lack a fair and substantial relationship to the legitimate purpose of eliminating double recoveries.

name: Winfree, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the HEIF is sweepable under the Cowper analysis because further appropriations are necessary to support expenditures, and declined to overrule Cowper precedent.

name: BORGHESAN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that while electronic monitoring creates a constitutionally protected liberty interest requiring due process for removal, the superior court lacked appellate jurisdiction because DOC's termination process was not an adjudicative proceeding, necessitating a remand to convert the appeal into a civil action.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Alaska Constitution implies an annual budgeting requirement, making forward-funded appropriations unconstitutional.

name: Borghesan, Justice
description: Did not participate in the case.

name: MAASSEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the superior court did not err in applying sentencing standards or considering deterrence and community condemnation, but abused its discretion by admitting police officer testimony and victim tribute videos without proper review, and that judge recusal was not warranted.

name: CARNEY, Justice
description: Concurred that the superior court properly considered sentencing benchmarks, aggravating factors, and that judge recusal was not necessary, and that admitting police officer testimony was an abuse of discretion. Dissented, arguing that the court's guidelines for victim tribute videos were insufficient and that the superior court abused its discretion by allowing emotionally charged videos and testimony, risking sentencing disparities based on victims' resources.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion of the court, upholding the tort duty, finding sufficient evidence for negligence, and affirming the application of the damages cap.

name: WINFREE, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the superior court correctly dismissed the lawsuit because injunctive relief claims presented non-justiciable political questions and declaratory relief claims were properly dismissed on prudential grounds.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the court should explicitly recognize a constitutional right to a livable climate and that declaratory relief would be a useful, albeit small, step in addressing climate change, and that the Kanuk analysis is no longer sound.

name: CARNEY, Justice
description: Dissented, joined Justice Maassen's dissenting opinion, arguing for the recognition of a constitutional right to a livable climate.

name: BOLGER, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the option to purchase dental insurance is an accrued benefit, but its value must be assessed by considering both coverage and premiums, thus vacating and remanding the lower court's decision.

name: WINFREE, Justice
description: Dissented, arguing that the legislature authorized discretionary, not mandatory, group health insurance benefits for retirees, and thus these benefits should not be constitutionally protected from diminishment.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Alaska Constitution requires an affirmative joint session vote for legislative confirmation or rejection of gubernatorial appointments, rendering statutory provisions that equate legislative inaction to rejection unconstitutional.

name: Bolger, Chief Justice
description: Did not participate in the case.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the superior court did not abuse its discretion in granting the preliminary injunction because the witness requirement impermissibly burdened the right to vote during the pandemic and the State's interests were not compelling enough to justify it.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, finding the recall application legally sufficient and emphasizing citizen access to the recall process.

name: STOWERS, Justice
description: Dissented, arguing that the governor's line-item vetoes were not legally sufficient grounds for recall and that the court overstepped its role.

name: Bolger, Chief Justice
description: Other, did not participate in the case.

name: BOLGER, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that granting the injunction would have jeopardized the prospects of a successful and timely election, and Galvin failed to show a clear probability of success on her constitutional claims.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the superior court should have issued the injunction, Galvin would likely succeed on her statutory claim, the public interest includes a proper ballot, and the evidence did not support that an injunction would seriously threaten an orderly election.

name: Borghesan, Justice
description: Did not participate in the case.

name: BOLGER, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the legislature could reasonably decide to treat misdemeanor traffic violations consistently to promote public safety while also protecting juvenile offenders from the harsh collateral consequences of a felony conviction, thus finding the statute constitutional.

name: STOWERS, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the juvenile court exclusion statute facially discriminates between minors accused of felony DUI and misdemeanor DUI, and that there is not a close relationship between the State's interests and the classification, thus violating equal protection rights.

name: MAASSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the statutory reinstatement right was an accrued benefit of the retirement system protected against diminishment or impairment by article XII, section 7, and its repeal was unconstitutional.

name: CARNEY, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the statutory right was not an accrued benefit protected by the constitution and Metcalfe, as a former member, was not covered by Article XII, Section 7.
